phases.description: Determine what is alive and reachable without over-scanning. Confirm discovered hosts are in scope before adding them as endpoints.

phases.name: Initial Host & Service Recon
phases.description: Run low-impact discovery: top ports, basic service and version detection, DNS and reverse DNS, TLS banners and obvious management planes. Add hosts and services as endpoints.

phases.name: Expanded Enumeration
phases.description: Do deeper enumeration where allowed: full TCP and UDP scans, service-specific enumeration, SMB, LDAP, NFS, SNMP, SSH, RDP, HTTP admin surfaces, certificate names and neighboring exposed services.

phases.name: Free Agentic Recon
phases.description: Check out the notes and then: Anything you think would make sense to do that is missing reconnaissance wise? Any tools to execute? Do not do anything that is not rerally needed!

steps.title: Free-form infrastructure recon based on notes
steps.description: Read GET /api/v1/notes. Decide if anything important is still missing reconnaissance-wise for this infrastructure: a service whose version wasn't pinned, a host whose role is unclear, a management interface that wasn't probed, a trust relationship that wasn't tested. Only act on real gaps and within the rules of engagement. If nothing is missing, finish this step with status=skipped and an observation explaining why.
steps.examples:
Targeted: a `-sV --version-intensity 7` follow-up on one port whose banner was ambiguous; an SMB null-session probe on one host where signing status was unknown.
Skipped: status=skipped, observations='Reachability + deeper enumeration already covered all in-scope hosts; service versions pinned; management surfaces mapped. No further recon needed.'

phases.name: Infrastructure Understanding
phases.description: Build a model of host roles, exposed trust boundaries, management networks, likely critical systems, authentication surfaces, shared services and segmentation points.

phases.name: Modify Checklist
phases.description: Disable irrelevant checks and add target-specific host or service checks based on discovered protocols, architecture, trust boundaries and allowed validation depth.

steps.title: Mark irrelevant checks as 'not applicable' (use the API — do NOT just take notes)
steps.description:
Actually modify the project checklist via the API. Do NOT just write your thoughts into the notes — that does not change the checklist. For every check that does not apply to this specific infrastructure, mark it `not applicable` with a one-line observation explaining why.

Use these endpoints (in this order):
  GET  /api/v1/checklist/titles                       — slim list: id, title, scope, category
  GET  /api/v1/checklist/filter?status=pending        — filter to only the ones still pending
  GET  /api/v1/check/{check_id}                       — full detail incl. description/examples
  PUT  /api/v1/check/{check_id}/status                — body: {"status": "not applicable"}
  PUT  /api/v1/check/{check_id}/observations          — body: {"observations": "why this does not apply"}

Finish this step only after you have gone through the checklist and acted on it. In observations of this step, summarise: how many checks you marked not-applicable and the rough categories.
steps.examples:
1) GET /api/v1/checklist/filter?status=pending&scope=global — review the global-checks first.
2) For each irrelevant one, e.g. an SMB-relay check on a network without any SMB services:
     PUT /api/v1/check/smb_relay_attack/status        body: {"status": "not applicable"}
     PUT /api/v1/check/smb_relay_attack/observations  body: {"observations": "No SMB (TCP/445) services discovered in scope."}
3) Repeat for service-specific checks that don't match the discovered protocols.
4) Finish this step:
     status='done', observations='Marked 9 checks NA (SMB family, NFS, LDAP-anon, SNMPv2c, IPMI) — rationale per check.'

phases.name: Work on Checklist
phases.description: Work through every 'global'-scope check on the project checklist. Pick a check, mark it focused via POST /api/v1/check/{id}/focus, set status + observations, then call POST /api/v1/check/{id}/finish. The phase advances only after every global-check is finished.

phases.description: Work host and service endpoints one by one, using the checklist for misconfigurations, default credentials, weak protocols, known CVEs, anonymous access and risky administration interfaces.

phases.description: From the findings so far, decide whether one service exposes credentials for another, management access implies lateral movement risk, discovered hostnames require more recon, or findings validate segmentation issues.
